title: A weekend without my phone
summary_es: Un fin de semana sin móvil. Verbos frecuentes, colocaciones y partículas.
text: Last month I decided to {{1}} a whole weekend without my phone. My friends didn't {{2}} me, but I was serious. On Saturday morning I felt strange. I kept {{3}} for my phone in my pocket, and I didn't know what time it was. So I went for a long walk and, for the first time in years, I really {{4}} attention to the streets around my flat. In the afternoon I read a book from beginning to end. By Sunday evening I felt more relaxed {{5}} I had for months. I'm not going to throw my phone away, but now I switch it {{6}} every Sunday.

gaps.explanation_es: El tiempo se «gasta» con spend: spend a weekend, spend two hours. «Pasar» no se traduce por pass aquí.
«Believe someone» = creer a alguien. «Agree» necesita with, y «think» no lleva una persona como complemento.
«Look for» = buscar. Tras «keep» el verbo va en -ing: I kept looking for it.
Colocación fija: «pay attention to» (prestar atención a). No se usa make ni do.
Comparativo: more relaxed than… «That» es el error típico por el «que» español.
«Switch off» = apagar. Con pronombre, va en medio: switch it off.
